finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(u, "OWNER") but discards its boolean result, so repo.wipe(tenant) runs for any caller regardless of role.
finding.source: Authenticated User u and tenant path parameter passed into wipe() (POST /tenants/{t}/wipe, src/Admin.java:24-25). Precondition: caller is authenticated but not OWNER.

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) entry point
requireRole(u, "OWNER") called as bare statement; return value unused
requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role) boolean and does not throw

finding.guards_checked: requireRole is non-throwing and its return value is discarded, so it gates nothing. No other authorization check exists between entry (line 25) and the sink (line 27) in this file. Contrast with export() at lines 31-33, which uses checkRole (throws) and is correctly gated. Route-layer auth middleware is not in the repo and could not be checked; the finding assumes only authentication is enforced upstream.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole at src/Admin.java:26 is the only role check on the wipe path, but it is a bare call whose boolean result is discarded (non-throwing per src/Admin.java:14-15). checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) would throw, but it is only used in export() at line 32, not wipe(). No other check exists between line 25 and the sink at line 27.
verdict.reason: At src/Admin.java:26 requireRole returns a boolean that is never tested, so repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 runs for any caller who reaches wipe(), including non-OWNER authenticated users. The only remaining caveat is that route-layer middleware is not in the repo, so an upstream OWNER check cannot be ruled out from this code alone, but nothing in the provided code blocks it.

finding.claim: export() (and wipe()) check the OWNER role globally but do not bind it to the target tenant, so an OWNER of one tenant may be able to export or wipe another tenant by supplying a different tenant path parameter.
finding.source: tenant path parameter (src/Admin.java:31 and 25) combined with the caller's global role set (User.roles, src/Admin.java:4). Precondition: caller holds OWNER in some tenant and supplies a different tenant id.
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) at src/Admin.java:33 and repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27.

trace.note: export(User u, String tenant) entry point
checkRole(u, "OWNER") checks global role set; User record has no tenant field
repo.export(tenant) uses the path tenant with no comparison to the user's tenant

finding.guards_checked: No tenant-membership or tenant-equality check appears in export() or wipe(). Role scoping is unknown from this file: if roles are tenant-scoped upstream or Repo.export filters by caller tenant, the finding does not hold. Repo implementation not in repo, so not verified.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) throws on a missing role and is called at line 32, so export() does enforce a global OWNER check. requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a bool, but its result is discarded at line 26, so wipe() has no effective check. No tenant-equality check exists in either method.
verdict.reason: The candidate's claim that wipe() checks OWNER is wrong: src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole as a bare statement and discards its bool, so wipe() at lines 25-27 performs no authorization and any caller can reach repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27. For export(), the cross-tenant premise is unsupported because User (src/Admin.java:4) has only a global role set with no tenant scoping, so an OWNER is OWNER everywhere in this code and the candidate's cross-tenant escalation is not demonstrated; the real defect in this file is the missing wipe() authorization, which should be re-reported separately.
